SI-4.answer: Mapping the Heterogeneous Phenotype of Schizophrenia and Bipolar Disorder Using Normative Models

NM2-1.detail: Gaussian process regression was used to estimate normative brain aging models. The models predicted regional gray and white matter volumes from age and sex. Cross-validation (10-fold) was performed on healthy individuals, and the trained model was applied to patients.
NM2-1.supporting_text: We estimated a normative brain aging model by using gaussian process regression to predict regional gray and white matter volumes across the brain from age and sex using voxel-based morphometry-derived gray and white matter maps. ... Normative models were estimated using gaussian process regression, yielding coherent measures of predictive confidence in addition to point estimates.

NM2-2.detail: Primary analysis used VBM-derived gray matter volume (GMV) and white matter volume (WMV) maps. Supplementary analyses additionally employed FreeSurfer-derived cortical thickness (CT) and pial area/surface area (SA) measures to better characterize volumetric differences in the cortex.
NM2-2.supporting_text: We estimated a normative brain aging model by using gaussian process regression to predict regional gray and white matter volumes across the brain from age and sex using voxel-based morphometry-derived gray and white matter maps. To supplement this analysis and to characterize volumetric differences more precisely, we also estimated normative models using Freesurfer-derived cortical thickness and pial area measures.

NM2-3.detail: Age and sex were used as the only explanatory variables (predictors) in the normative models. These covariates were used consistently across both VBM-based and FreeSurfer-based analyses.
NM2-3.supporting_text: We estimated a normative brain aging model by using gaussian process regression to predict regional gray and white matter volumes across the brain from age and sex... We used age and gender as a predictor for these brain features, using the normative modelling approach described in the main text.
